harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 so every sudo-executed command is recorded (user, timestamp, command) to /var/log/sudo-commands.log via a sudoers Defaults directive, while disabling sudo's syslog output so entries no longer reach /var/log/auth.log or /var/log/syslog. Verified with both root and a disposable test user, then performed the mandatory single-node restart, confirming boot identity changed and the logging configuration/log file/functionality survived and continued working post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected existing rsyslog rules and sudo build defaults (facility authpriv) on node1
Wrote /etc/sudoers.d/99-sudo-logfile with Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log", Defaults log_year, and Defaults !syslog; validated with visudo -cf before and after install
Verified new sudo invocations (as root) appear only in the dedicated log with timestamp/user/command and no longer append COMMAND= lines to auth.log/syslog

Created a temporary NOPASSWD test user sudologtest, ran a sudo command as that user, confirmed the log correctly attributed the non-root username, then fully removed the test user and temporary sudoers file
Captured baseline boot_id, uptime, rsyslog status, sudoers config, and log line count on node1
Issued a backgrounded shutdown -r now so the ack returned before disconnect, then polled until node1 was reachable again
Confirmed changed boot_id and new uptime -s value proving an actual restart occurred

Post-restart verified rsyslog active, sudoers config intact, log file persisted with prior entries plus new appended entries, and re-ran a sudo command confirming continued exclusive logging to the dedicated file

evidence.requirement: Every sudo command logged with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
evidence.summary: Log file created, sudoers Defaults logfile/log_year config validated and installed, and entries captured showing 'Sep 5 00:05:xx 2026 : root/sudologtest : PWD=... USER=root ; COMMAND=...' for both root and a test user.

evidence.requirement: Sudo command entries kept out of the general system log
evidence.summary: Defaults !syslog disabled sudo's syslog logging; COMMAND= line count in /var/log/auth.log stayed frozen at 7 (all pre-dating the config) across further sudo invocations, and /var/log/syslog had 0 COMMAND= entries throughout, while new sudo activity kept appearing only in the dedicated file.
Temporary NOPASSWD sudo user sudologtest created, sudo id run as that user logged with 'sudologtest' as the acting user, then user and temp sudoers file fully removed.
Captured boot_id bdd5de93-e94e-4d33-8384-6a01c51a3d49, uptime, active rsyslog, sudoers config content, and 24-line log file as pre-restart baseline.
Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' returned acknowledgement before the connection dropped; immediate follow-up probe failed with connection reset, confirming the node went down for restart.

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed after restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id read as 17065b78-02a9-472a-ac2d-4cbb64e08146, differing from the pre-restart baseline, proving an actual reboot occurred.

evidence.requirement: Node1 post-restart recovery of required service/data (sudo command logging)
evidence.summary: After reboot, uptime -s showed a new boot time, rsyslog was active, the sudoers config file was intact, the log file persisted with prior entries plus new appended lines, and a fresh sudo command continued to log only to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with no new auth.log COMMAND= entries.
